headline.caveat: Contract dollars undisclosed. SK Hynix is NVIDIA's lead HBM supplier — reported ~2/3 of HBM4 supply — with output effectively sold out through 2026 and customers (incl. NVIDIA) prepaying for capacity.

realized_to_date.caveat: Ongoing multi-year purchases; SK Hynix does not disclose customer-level revenue, though NVIDIA is understood to be its largest customer by far.

nature_md: Multi-year HBM supply relationship: SK Hynix has led every HBM generation qualification at NVIDIA (HBM3, HBM3E, HBM4 for Rubin) and reportedly holds ~two-thirds of NVIDIA's HBM4 allocation. HBM output is sold out through 2026 under LTAs with customer prepayments — memory has become a contracted, prepaid commodity rather than a spot market, a defining feature of the 2026 memory super-cycle. Terms (pricing, volumes) are undisclosed; the Stargate memory LOI (up to 900K DRAM wafers/mo with Samsung+SK) is a separate OpenAI-side arrangement.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: NVIDIA's HBM purchases flow through COGS as systems ship; capacity prepayments to memory vendors sit in prepaid/supply-commitment disclosures (aggregated, not itemized by supplier).
accounting.payee_treatment_md: SK Hynix books revenue on delivery under LTAs; prepayments are contract liabilities funding capex (M15X, Yongin). HBM's contracted nature underpinned record 2026 margins — and its concentration risk: a handful of AI customers dominate the book.

observations.notes: ~2/3 per Korean supply-chain reporting; neither company confirms.
